content.text:
**Not fully complete, but you had a substantial working prototype by 5–6 October 2026.** You’ve expanded well beyond the assignment while a few original requirements remain unfinished.

**The clearest milestone is 6 October, 1:21 AM IST.** Clanker completed a real Google login using privately collected credentials, an SMS-code handoff, automatic resumption and independent verification. The previous day, saved-password reuse in a fresh browser had passed on a controlled website. [Verification record](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/verification/evidence/2026-10-05-google-login-e2e.md:46)

I would call that **“core POC working,”** rather than give you a false assignment-completion date.

The remaining reasons are concrete:

- **Automatic authenticator login still lacks decisive live proof.** The implementation exists, but today’s GitHub tests haven’t verified an actual fresh TOTP challenge completed using the saved seed. [Current evidence](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/clanker-qa/batches/2026-10-11-reliability-round6/CAMPAIGN.json:331)
- **The final handoff isn’t verified.** Clean-checkout setup, reviewer access and the finished demo remain open in the submission records; the README still contains demo placeholders. [Checklist](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/docs/SUBMISSION.md:7)

Those matter because the brief asks for a working experience plus a runnable repo, deployed access, a short demo and an access-management note: :codex-file-citation{path="/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Downloads/Zonko Labs Engineering Assignment.pdf" purpose="source"}

**The “because why not?” work falls into five groups:**

1. **Turning it into a multiuser Slack product.** Automatic onboarding when someone joins, personal profiles, shared-channel routing, concurrent users and welcome messages. Your own scope explicitly identifies this as additional behavior. **October 4–5 onward.** [Scope](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/production/V1_SCOPE.md:21)

2. **Building a team collaboration assistant.** Moving channel tasks into private DMs, returning public updates to the correct thread, recalling earlier conversations, preserving multiple people’s preferences and updating shared offsite plans. **October 6–11.** [Recall work](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/docs/decisions/2026-10-08-user-scoped-slack-recall.md:9)

3. **Expanding the vault into sharing and personal profiles.** Teammate invitations, credential-by-credential grants, recipient notifications, plus reusable addresses, phone numbers, names, DOB and gender with consent controls. These go beyond basic saved website access. **October 6–8 onward.** [Sharing](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/docs/decisions/2026-10-06-vault-invitations.md:3) · [Personal profiles](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/docs/decisions/2026-10-08-personal-identity.md:3)

4. **Adding product and presentation polish.** Working indicators, acknowledgement reactions, editing messages to revise tasks, a consistent Clanker persona, branding, and elaborate 4K/60fps demo production. A short demo was required; that production depth was your addition. **October 6 onward.** [Message-edit behavior](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/docs/decisions/2026-10-06-slack-message-edits.md:27)

5. **Building infrastructure around the product.** A 12-scenario, multiple-user QA system with parallel repair campaigns; browser-profile migration and concurrency machinery; and exploration of cloud workers, VM pools and autoscaling. The cloud architecture remains deferred. **Throughout the project, especially October 10–11.** [Benchmark](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/docs/CLANKER_BENCHMARK.md:3) · [Deferred architecture](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/production/README.md:3)

**The expansion and the remaining assignment fixes have happened in parallel.** TOTP, secure reuse, revocation, recovery and checking actual results were always part of the assignment, so I wouldn’t label all work after October 6 as optional.
